title: Asteroid Collision
summary: A row of asteroids is given as a list of nonzero integers `asteroids`. The absolute value is an asteroid's size and the sign its direction: positive moves right, negative moves left, all at the same speed. When a right-mover and a left-mover collide, the smaller one is destroyed; equal sizes destroy each other. Asteroids moving the same way never meet. Return the asteroids that survive, in their original order.

examples.explanation: 7 destroys -3. Then -9 destroys 4, then 7, and keeps flying left; 2 flies right, away from it.
-4 flies left with nothing ahead of it. -6 destroys 1, then meets 6, which has the same size, so both are destroyed.

approaches.twist: Push each asteroid, but let a left-mover pop smaller right-movers off the top until it is destroyed, ties, or none are left.
Scan the row for a right-mover followed directly by a left-mover, settle that crash, and rescan until no such pair is left.
approaches.note: Works, but a pass may settle only one crash before the rescan, so it takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: A left-mover first hits the nearest right-mover before it, the most recent survivor still flying: the top of the stack.
A left-mover that wins keeps flying into the next right-mover, so pop in a loop until it loses, ties, or finds none.

signals.phrase: moving the same way never meet
signals.meaning: Only a right-mover on top and a new left-mover can crash; every other asteroid is simply pushed.
Survivors sit on the stack from left to right, so the stack itself is the answer.

constraintReading: Up to 10⁴ asteroids: settling one crash per pass and rescanning the row is O(n²), up to about 10⁸ steps, too slow in Python. With a stack, each asteroid is pushed once and popped at most once, so one pass is O(n); the stack can hold every asteroid, so the space is O(n).

related.relation: Also pops in a while loop as long as the new item beats the top, but here only a left-mover pops, and a tie destroys both.
